headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Haystack’s MCP/networked RAG surface paired with LightZero’s local-only, non-writing runtime.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes REST APIs and MCP servers with broad network egress, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content and pass it onward. LightZero has no MCP or filesystem write surface, so the main pathway is Haystack output being treated as instructions by the pair’s orchestration rather than a direct bidirectional bridge. The interaction is plausible in default integrations, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack is connected to an MCP server that returns untrusted content
IF LightZero consumes Haystack output as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints for untrusted sources
Add provenance tags to Haystack outputs
Require human review before forwarding retrieved text
Restrict Haystack to allowlisted APIs
requires-engineering: add instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack can send data over broad network egress and may expose retrieved content to external services, while LightZero is local-only with no network egress and no data classes touched. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling evidence, so leakage between the pair is limited unless the operator routes sensitive documents into Haystack. The blast radius is small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are indexed or queried through Haystack
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to third-party APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive corpora out of Haystack
Use a local-only backend for retrieval
Disable external API connectors
Review logs for document snippets
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive indexes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has network egress and MCP access, but LightZero explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, subprocess, shell, and network egress. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF LightZero is granted new write or network permissions outside this profile
mitigations: Keep LightZero in its current read-only mode
Do not mount shared writable volumes
Avoid granting git or shell access
requires-engineering: add explicit locking if write scopes are introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent, so its outputs are likely to be treated as retrieved facts, while LightZero is a game-playing system that can consume upstream outputs in an orchestrated pipeline. The pair lacks documented verification or critique steps, so erroneous Haystack retrievals could cascade into LightZero-driven decisions or evaluations. The pathway exists in default integrations, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF LightZero consumes Haystack-generated text as authoritative input
IF no verification step checks Haystack retrievals before downstream use
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require citations for all Haystack claims
Flag low-confidence retrievals for review
Limit LightZero to advisory outputs
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no network egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data flowing into Haystack and being transmitted externally. LightZero is not cited further because it has no relevant compliance surface here.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed through Haystack
IF external transmission occurs without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Haystack
Confirm data-processing terms for external APIs
Turn off telemetry where possible
Document retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
